arguments.topic: video frame segmentation endoscopy deep learning

rows.title: Multi-Frame Feature Aggregation for Real-Time Instrument Segmentation in Endoscopic Video
rows.method: Recurrent Multi-frame Feature Aggregation (MFFA) with a lightweight encoder and synthetic frame-sequence training
rows.summary: Aggregates temporal and spatial frame features to reduce computation and improve surgical instrument segmentation over corresponding deeper models.

rows.title: An objective comparison of detection and segmentation algorithms for artefacts in clinical endoscopy.
rows.method: Benchmark comparison of 23 artefact detection and segmentation algorithms, including deep learning strategies
rows.summary: Benchmarks artefact detection, segmentation, and generalization, finding that deep learning methods rank highest but no method leads across all tasks.

rows.title: Application of Convolutional Neural Networks for Automated Ulcer Detection in Wireless Capsule Endoscopy Images.
rows.method: AlexNet and GoogLeNet convolutional neural networks
rows.summary: Evaluates CNNs for ulcer versus non-ulcer classification and reports superior performance over traditional machine learning methods.

rows.title: Deep learning for real-time detection of nasopharyngeal carcinoma during nasopharyngeal endoscopy.
rows.dataset: private cohort (2,429 frames from 690 patients across three medical centers)
rows.metric_values: Internal: precision 0.977; recall 0.943; mAP 0.977; F1 0.960. External: precision 0.825; recall 0.743; mAP 0.814; F1 0.780. Evaluation at IoU 0.5; inference speed 52.9 FPS
rows.summary: Develops a real-time nasopharyngeal carcinoma detector to support early identification and biopsy site selection.

rows.title: 3D-semantic segmentation and classification of stomach infections using uncertainty aware deep neural networks
rows.method: DeepLabv3 and ResNet-50 semantic segmentation with pretrained ResNet-50 feature extraction and uncertainty-aware classification
rows.summary: Proposes stomach infection segmentation and classification with uncertainty estimation and model interpretability.

rows.title: A novel solution of deep learning for endoscopic ultrasound image segmentation: enhanced computer aided diagnosis of gastrointestinal stromal tumor
rows.method: Multi-scale Gaussian kernel fuzzy clustering and vector field convolution for segmentation; CNN with Class Activation Mapping for diagnosis
rows.metric_values: Accuracy increased from 84.275% to 88.4%; processing time reduced from 28.525% to 24.575% (percentages as reported)
rows.summary: Combines automatic region-of-interest segmentation with CNN diagnosis to improve tumor image clarity and accuracy while reducing processing time.

rows.title: Bleeding detection in wireless capsule endoscopy videos - Color versus texture features.
rows.journal: Journal of applied clinical medical physics
rows.method: Color and texture feature extraction with machine-learning classifiers
rows.summary: Combines color and texture features to classify bleeding frames and segment bleeding areas at the pixel level.

rows.title: Segmentation of Bleeding Regions in Wireless Capsule Endoscopy for Detection of Informative Frames
rows.method: Simplified multilayer perceptron and convolutional neural network using selected color channels
rows.summary: Simplifies neural networks for bleeding-region segmentation inside capsule devices, trading CNN accuracy against lower MLP computation.

rows.title: Inter- and Intraobserver Variability in Bowel Preparation Scoring for Colon Capsule Endoscopy: Impact of AI-Assisted Assessment Feasibility Study.
rows.method: TransUNet segmentation model with a custom Patch Loss function for AI-assisted CC-CLEAR scoring
rows.dataset: CESCAIL study cohort (25 videos selected from 673 participants)
rows.metric_values: Manual Leighton-Rex: Fleiss' kappa 0.14; ICC 0.55. Manual CC-CLEAR: Fleiss' kappa 0.27; ICC 0.90. AI-assisted CC-CLEAR: Fleiss' kappa 0.27; ICC 0.69; less experienced readers: Fleiss' kappa 0.15; ICC 0.56. Intraobserver ICC > 0.75 for experienced readers and 0.03–0.80 for others. AI-assisted scores lower by 1.46 points (p < 0.001)
rows.summary: Evaluates AI-assisted bowel cleanliness scoring, finding moderate overall interobserver agreement and lower scores than manual assessment.

rows.title: Predicting semantic segmentation quality in laryngeal endoscopy images.
rows.method: Automatic segmentation-quality prediction with traffic-light quality flagging; architecture not stated
rows.summary: Predicts glottal segmentation quality using IoU with performance comparable to human raters and flags problematic frames for human review.
